links.outcome: Performance of zero/one-shot versus fine-tuned open-source LLMs on local labeled data, by training data size
links.effect: Fine-tuned open-source LLMs achieved higher F1-scores than GPT4 models; gains plateaued at 25% of training data (5,718 impressions) and were comparable at 5% (1,144 impressions).
links.quote: However, fine-tuned open-source LLMs achieved higher F1-scores than GPT4 models.

links.outcome: Comparison of open-source LLMs against GPT4 models on the same data for radiophenotype extraction
links.effect: GPT4-turbo/GPT4o outperformed open-source LLMs zero/one-shot; fine-tuned Mistral0.2 had OR 0.27 (95% CI 0.20-0.36) versus best GPT4 for progression, favoring the fine-tuned models.
links.quote: In zero-/one-shot settings, GPT4-turbo/GPT4o outperformed open-source LLMs.

unlisted_practices: Fine-tuning small open-source LLMs on small labeled sets as an alternative to proprietary LLMs for clinical information extraction

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the performance of various LLMs (zero-shot, few-shot, fine-tuned) for extracting phenotypic data from radiology report impressions. It evaluates model accuracy and fine-tuning data sample efficiency rather than testing an operational deployment practice or safeguard.
